_why: The check's whole value is noticing an install that still loads while lying about its contents. It did that for h-mad and, for 68 days, not for its neighbour -- a correct h-mad symlink beside a `handoff` directory copied in June, with the check reporting PASS over it. Every mutation here restores one spelling of 'a correct h-mad vouches for the rest', because each fails in the same silent direction: the stale copy keeps loading and nothing says so.

mutations.name: the-sibling-root-is-the-skill-not-the-repo
mutations._mechanism: The live defect at its source. `~/.claude/skills/h-mad` resolves to the repo's h-mad SUBDIRECTORY, so globbing there walks h-mad's own subfolders, matches no SKILL.md and vouches for a checkout never looked at. Every unit test passed against a fixture that made this invisible; only a test shaped like a real install can see it.
mutations.find: checkout.parent if checkout is not None else None
mutations.replace: checkout if checkout is not None else None

mutations.name: a-copied-sibling-is-not-reported
mutations._mechanism: Treat a real directory as acceptable. This is the 68-day bug restored exactly: the copy loads, drifts arbitrarily far from the checkout, and the check calls it healthy.

mutations.name: a-sibling-from-another-checkout-passes
mutations._mechanism: SPLIT_INSTALL one directory over: the link resolves and the skill loads, from a tree nobody is editing. Dropping the target comparison makes any symlink acceptable.

mutations.name: an-uninstalled-skill-is-reported-as-broken
mutations._mechanism: The converse failure: drop the not-installed skip and every skill in the checkout the operator chose NOT to install becomes an issue. A check that cries wolf on a healthy install gets ignored, which costs the real finding.
mutations.find:
if not link.is_symlink() and not link.exists():
            continue

mutations.name: the-checkout-is-compared-against-itself
mutations._mechanism: Drop the same-directory guard and a checkout that IS the skills directory reports every skill as a copy of itself -- issues that name real paths and mean nothing.
